faqs.q: Where and how are the Parker 12AT series low pressure filters used?
faqs.a: Parker 12AT series low pressure filters are spin-on filters for petroleum-based fluids, with an aluminium head, NPTF ports and a paper element. The maker states 150 psi (10 bar) and a temperature of 225 °F, and the listing carries 4 part numbers.

faqs.q: What part numbers are listed for the Parker 12AT series low pressure filters?
faqs.a: The Parker 12AT series low pressure filters are listed as 4 part numbers, for example 12AT03CN15BBH, 12AT110CBPCN12H and 12AT110CBPCS12H. Quote the part number, or the size you need, and we confirm the match before supply.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right size or model of the Parker 12AT series low pressure filters?
faqs.a: Choose the model by the element size in the part number, such as 12AT03CN15BBH and 12AT10BN15BBH, and the port size. The 12AT is interchangeable with major brands of the same size, and its dual Buna N seals keep the outer seal tight to 150 psi.

faqs.q: What pressure rating do the Parker 12AT series low pressure filters have?
faqs.a: Parker states 150 psi (10 bar) for the 12AT series and a temperature of 225 °F, with an outer seal that resists leaks up to 150 psi. It is a low pressure filter, so do not use it on a pressure line.

faqs.q: Which materials are the Parker 12AT series low pressure filters offered in?
faqs.a: The 12AT has an aluminium head, paper filter media and dual Buna N seals, with an outer seal that resists leaks to 150 psi and an inner seal that keeps incoming fluid from mixing with filtered fluid. Buna N suits petroleum-based fluids.

faqs.q: Which standards apply to the Parker 12AT series low pressure filters?
faqs.a: The listing names no ISO or SAE standard for the Parker 12AT series low pressure filters and holds no certificates. Filtration ratings are normally set by the ISO 16889 multi-pass test and oil cleanliness is reported as an ISO 4406 code, but the listing gives neither a beta rating nor a code, so ask in the enquiry if you need the maker's test data.

faqs.q: What do the Parker 12AT series low pressure filters connect to?
faqs.a: The Parker 12AT series low pressure filters screw onto a filter base or head with a matching thread and gasket, so match the part number to the base. Quote the part number of the filter being replaced, or the thread, height and diameter, and we confirm the match before supply.

faqs.q: How do I fit and look after the Parker 12AT series low pressure filters?
faqs.a: Replace the Parker 12AT series low pressure filters on the maker's schedule or when the indicator shows it is clogged. Oil the gasket, spin it on by hand to the gasket plus the turn the maker advises, and check for leaks after restarting. Do not over-tighten, since the filter has to come off again.

faqs.q: Where are the Parker 12AT series low pressure filters used?
faqs.a: The Parker 12AT series low pressure filters are used as replacement hydraulic and transmission filters on mobile machines and trucks, where a spin-on filter is quick to change in the field.

faqs.q: How do the Parker 12AT series low pressure filters differ from the Parker 15CN series medium pressure filters?
faqs.a: The 12AT is a low pressure spin-on filter rated 150 psi in 4 part numbers, while [the Parker 15CN series medium pressure filters](/p/parker-15cn-series-medium-pressure-filters) are medium pressure filters with a replaceable element in 8 part numbers. Choose the 12AT for low-pressure return and lube lines.
